<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/formula`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **35** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/formula/src/index.ts`, `packages/lint/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/email-templates.mdx`  _(via MAIL_TEMPLATE_FORMATTERS (symbol, a top-level const object), opportunity.stage (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via AUTHORING_RULES (symbol, a top-level const object))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/formula/src/index.ts`, `packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **221** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e00bcc6aeaf56c339598ef49306ed3ca90d781de` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `403d623e7b2e72ed45587e804bd09391f7c742b0` — the merge of head `98f61ec65b298cd6e78f38e3e5600a92e7c35861` into base `e00bcc6aeaf56c339598ef49306ed3ca90d781de`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 403d623e7b2e72ed45587e804bd09391f7c742b0 && git checkout 403d623e7b2e72ed45587e804bd09391f7c742b0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e00bcc6aeaf56c339598ef49306ed3ca90d781de 98f61ec65b298cd6e78f38e3e5600a92e7c35861 && git checkout -B drift-repro e00bcc6aeaf56c339598ef49306ed3ca90d781de && git merge --no-ff 98f61ec65b298cd6e78f38e3e5600a92e7c35861

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e00bcc6aeaf56c339598ef49306ed3ca90d781de
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e00bcc6aeaf56c339598ef49306ed3ca90d781de` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `29f86544672c75be2a2cc6a836756ed2ce74fbae`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/email-template.zod.ts + packages/formula/src/mail-hole-grammar.ts, packages/formula/src/template-engine.ts, packages/formula/src/index.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-email-template-hole-grammar.ts, packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts (widened by the seat: the spec sentence quotes the formula constant word for word, and the window question lives in the renderer's formatter). Cited and read, not reviewed: packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/template-engine.ts (the first consumer), packages/lint/src/validate-object-references.ts, packages/lint/src/object-graph.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts, packages/formula/src/stdlib.ts. The lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT: the two new test files, the moved unknown-formatter pin, the three changesets, the two docs pages.

### ① Derived judgments

- Mail dialect accept-set (`judgeHoleFormatter(…, 'mail')`, `parseMailHole`, `judgeMailHoleGrammar`): `option:object.field` is accepted — right, parameter 1 of ruling F (6670405874) in the seat's spelling (6671557736): bare, no quotes, no `@path`. `optionFieldReference` (template-engine.ts:283) reads the argument as written, the `currencyCodePath` reading, so a quoted or `@`-marked form is not a reference; `OPTION_FIELD_RE` is one word, a dot, one word, so no dot, two dots, an empty side and inner whitespace are `option-field-shape` (template-engine.ts:513), naming the hole, the argument as written and `OPTION_ARGUMENT_RULE`. `option : opportunity.stage` is accepted (both sides trimmed, the `currency :EUR` reading). Right.
- In-app dialect accept-set: `known` is `TEMPLATE_FORMATTERS`, the eleven, unchanged (template-engine.ts:476); `option` is `known-formatter` with the mail-only clause (:499); the in-app `parseHole` reaches the shared judge before `FORMATTERS[name]`, so compile, `validateExpression` and evaluate all refuse it, and `os validate` refuses a notify title / message and an action confirmText. Right, parameter 2. Public-surface change: the in-app sentence for `option` moved from the generic "holes are a field path" refusal to known-formatter — still a compile refusal; nothing that compiled stops compiling. Right.
- `currency:@path` unchanged: the currency arm of the judge is untouched, `codePath` and `optionField` are computed independently in `parseMailHole`, `MAIL_ONLY_FORMATTERS` is `['option']` (:180). Right.
- `MAIL_TEMPLATE_FORMATTERS` is `Object.keys(FORMATTERS)` with `option` declared last (:190), so the mail known-formatters list ends `json, option` and the in-app list is unchanged; the spec sentence "naming the known formatters" holds in both dialects; the unknown-formatter lint pin moved to the mail list. Right.
- Lint arm (parameter 4): `optionFieldIndex` (validate-email-template-hole-grammar.ts:99-111) over `objectsAsServed` plus the injected columns, options read by `declaresOptionsOnceServed` so a `picklist` name counts; at the publish door `stack.objects` is the live universe the gate carries (`CONTEXT_STACK_KEY_ORDER`). Right for the app's own objects; the CLI doors resolve the object against `stack.objects` only — ④ should-fix.
- Arm under the existing rule id: no `rule-explanations.ts` entry exists for `email-template-hole-grammar`, so nothing there is stale. Right.
- Exports (index.ts:69-75 and the types): `MAIL_TEMPLATE_FORMATTERS`, `OPTION_ARGUMENT_RULE`, `optionFieldReference`, `OptionLabelTable`, `OptionFieldReference`; `TemplateHoleGrammarRule` gains four members; `formatValue` gains an optional `optionLabels`. All additive. Right.
- `judgeMailHoleGrammar` with no `objects` (plugin-email at render) does not judge the reference — right for this half; the server half judges it with the served definition (parameter 3).
- Wrong: the `option` formatter's no-table branch (template-engine.ts:166-173) — ④ must-fix.

### ② Semver level

Three changesets, all `minor`: spec (one additive describe sentence), formula (a new formatter, new exports, an optional parameter, a union widened by new members — the `currency-code-path-undeclared` widening shipped as minor in 18.3.0), lint (an arm under an existing rule id that refuses only holes main already refused as known-formatter). `Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the PR body and all three changesets — right: every template accepted on main is accepted unchanged; the only holes whose verdict moves are `option` holes, refused on main at every door. `Metadata-protocol: added` — right, a new formatter in the published template grammar. The ④ must-fix does not move the level: refusing a render that has no table is still a widening against main, where every such hole is refused at authoring and at send.

### ③ Boundary flags

- os-dev-report (6672443566) `open_questions[0]`, the window — answered in ④ as the must-fix: the tree itself, not only the landing order, must not print a value the published sentence does not describe. With the fix in, holding the landing is the seat's queue call under its own claim (a validate-then-refuse window is a hold), not the only honest answer.
- `open_questions[1]`, arm or new rule id — keep the arm: the rule owns the hole, one hole gets one verdict, and no explanation entry exists to go stale.
- `out_of_scope_findings[0]`, CLI doors vs publish door ("noted, not filed") — escalated: ④ should-fix.
- `Skills-docs: follow-up owed` (parameter 6) — the seat files the card; not a finding here.
- Docs drift check: `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx` via `AUTHORING_RULES` — prose outside `hits`, the lane seat's.
- Check-runs on the head at review time: 24 success (Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check PR Size, Check Documentation Links, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Plan Test Core shards, Flag docs affected, Auto Label, filter), 8 skipped (opt-in harnesses and matrix shards), 30 still pending: Build Core / Docs / UI Deps, Test Core 1-8, Type Check ×4, Lint · ESLint, docs & code guards, repo & tooling, CI release & engine, the two scoped lint jobs, Live E2E UI. This record relies on the green ones and names the pending ones as pending; nothing was re-run.

### ④ Design judgment

`hits`: packages/spec/src/system/email-template.zod.ts:126-129, the `OPTION_ARGUMENT_RULE` sentence. Against the ruling it implements (F, parameters 1, 2, 4, the spec side of 5): holds — it states the formatter, the mail-only scope, the bare `object.field`, the object / field / options condition, and parameter 3's "outside the options prints as stored", and the formula test pins the three faces quote the constant. Against its first consumer at this head: does not hold.

**MUST-FIX** — packages/formula/src/template-engine.ts:166-173 (the `option` formatter), with packages/formula/src/template-option-formatter.test.ts:185 (the ⭐ pin "with no table … prints the value as stored") and the published sentence at email-template.zod.ts:126. With no table for its `object.field`, the formatter prints the stored value and nothing signals it. The first consumer, plugin-email's render (packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/template-engine.ts:161), passes no `optionLabels` at this head, so a hole that passes every authoring door prints `needs_analysis` to the en-US and the zh-CN recipient where the sentence `@objectstack/spec` publishes says the label — the dev measured exactly that. That is a capability the spec declares and the tree does not deliver, and this grammar's own precedent refuses the shape: `currency` with no argument and no tenant default throws (template-engine.ts:99-104, "never picks a currency"), plugin-email judges it before `formatValue` and sends nothing (plugin-email template-engine.ts:147), and the dialect note that justifies refusing `option` in-app says why — "an in-app slot has no such table" (template-engine.ts:220-228). A mail render with no table is the same situation and gets the opposite answer. After the server half lands the branch stays reachable by any render path that does not prefetch, and the recipient then silently reads the stored value with no log line: the hotcrm#2391 symptom back, behind a hole the spec says is labelled.
Fix, inside this PR's surface: the `option` formatter refuses when `optionLabels` holds no entry for its `object.field` — throw as `currency` does, carrying an exported sentence (`optionTableRefusal`, the `currencyDefaultRefusal` shape, so the server half can judge it before `formatValue` and prefix `TEMPLATE_INVALID`); flip the pin at test.ts:185 to the refusal; the formatter comment (:161-165), the formula changeset's "with no table … prints as stored" bullet and the docs paragraph (content/docs/automation/email-templates.mdx:164-166) say the render is refused, never the stored value. A value the table does not hold still prints as stored (parameter 3, pinned at test.ts:170-173). Then in the window the hole's send outcome is the one main gives it today — refused, nothing sent — and no release prints a value the sentence does not describe; whether this half lands before the server half is green is then the seat's call under claim 6671557736 (a template that validates and then refuses at send is a hold there too), and holding is no longer the only honest answer.

**SHOULD-FIX** — packages/lint/src/validate-email-template-hole-grammar.ts:99-111 (`optionFieldIndex`) and packages/formula/src/mail-hole-grammar.ts:176-180 (`option-object-unknown`). At the CLI doors the object is resolved against `stack.objects` (plus `objectExtensions`) only. The repo's object-reference ladder (validate-object-references.ts:61-78, rung ① at :256) also resolves an object an entry of this artifact's `packages[]` provides (ADR-0130 D4) and a platform-prefixed name in `PLATFORM_PROVIDED_OBJECT_NAMES` (rung ③), and the list-view rule leaves an unresolved binding unjudged at the CLI doors because it "may be a dependency package's object the stack does not carry" (rule-explanations.ts:3854-3857). Here `{{ status | option:sys_user.status }}`, or a hole naming a sibling package's object, is an `error` at `os validate`, `os build` and `os lint` saying the app "does not have" an object it has, while the publish door accepts the same template from the live universe. The dev noted it as out of scope; the sentence "the object is one the app has" is the ladder's reading, not the stack array's. Fix: build the index over rung ① (own objects and the `packages[]` objects, whose fields are in hand) and, for a rung-③ name, leave the field unjudged at the CLI doors (the publish door and the server half's `TEMPLATE_INVALID` judge it with the served definition); the refusal sentence then names the ladder as `object-reference-unknown` does. Pin both cases in validate-email-template-hole-grammar.option.test.ts.

**SHOULD-FIX** — email-template.zod.ts:126-129: the sentence says "the select option whose value it holds" and is silent on the multi-select reading the formatter has (template-engine.ts:172: each element labelled, joined with `, `; pinned at test.ts:175; stated only in the formula changeset). One clause in `OPTION_ARGUMENT_RULE`, so the three quoting surfaces carry it; otherwise the published grammar does not say what a `multiselect` hole prints.

Tried and holding: `option` with no argument, `option:`, `option:stage`, `option:'x.y'`, `option:"x.y"`, `option:@x`, `option:@x.y`, `option:a.b.c`, `option:.b`, `option:a.`, `option:a. b` → `option-field-shape`, naming the hole, the argument as written and the rule; `Option:…` and `optoin` → `known-formatter`, the mail list ending `option`; `{{ x | option:a.b | upper }}` → `one-formatter`; `option:__proto__.x` → unknown object (a Map lookup), and both table reads are own-property guarded; a lookup path (`option:opportunity.account.industry`) is two dots, refused by design; a text field → `option-field-no-options`; a `picklist`-bound field and an `objectExtensions` field → accepted; case is exact on object and field names, as everywhere in the stack; each in-app surface (notify title and message at `os validate`, action confirmText, compile / `validateExpression` / evaluate) refuses with the mail-only clause; the `currency:@path` reading is unchanged.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-d8v0qv`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L6bhgVugtCCwBs98FeR27P`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

Cited and read, not reviewed: packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/template-engine.ts and email-service.ts (the first consumer, unchanged), packages/lint/src/validate-object-references.ts, packages/lint/src/object-graph.ts. The lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT: the two test files, the three changesets, the two docs pages.

Delta review over `29f86544` (record 6672632729, which this one carries for everything the delta did not touch). `git diff 29f86544 d73ae610 --stat`: one commit, 12 files — the three changesets, the two docs pages, formula index.ts / mail-hole-grammar.ts / template-engine.ts and its test, the lint rule and its option test, the spec file. authoring-rules.ts, the moved unknown-formatter pin and plugin-email did not move; nothing outside the round-1 file list moved.

### ① Derived judgments

- Mail accept-set: unchanged from round 1 — `option:object.field` bare, the eleven shape refusals, `known-formatter` listing `option`, `currency:@path` untouched (the delta does not touch `judgeHoleFormatter`, `optionFieldReference`, `parseMailHole` or the currency arm). Carried.
- In-app refusal: unchanged, carried.
- Render accept-set (template-engine.ts:169-176): an `option` hole renders only when the caller's table holds its `object.field`; otherwise `formatValue` throws a `RangeError` carrying `optionTableRefusal` (:284-300, exported at index.ts). Right — the must-fix's shape, the `currency` precedent (:99-104). A value the table does not hold still prints as stored, a multi-select labels each element joined with `, `, a missing value prints empty (the pins at test.ts:170-193 are unchanged). Right, parameter 3.
- Lint object resolution (validate-email-template-hole-grammar.ts:124-141): own objects as served (fields judged), then objects an entry of this artifact's `packages[]` provides via `packagesOf` (the ADR-0130 D4 `{ manifest }` shape, fields judged; a stack name wins), then every `PLATFORM_PROVIDED_OBJECT_NAMES` entry not already indexed as `null` (resolves, field unjudged). The grammar's `objects` type admits `null` and returns no finding for it (mail-hole-grammar.ts:166, :185); the unknown-object refusal names the three rungs (:180). Formula and lint agree on the same inputs: `sys_user.status` → resolved, unjudged (both pinned: formula test.ts:124, lint test.ts:91); `sys_userz.status` → `option-object-unknown` in both (lint test.ts:94-95); a sibling package's object → fields judged, its text field `option-field-no-options` (lint test.ts:84). Right. One divergence from the ladder it names — ④ should-fix.

### ② Semver level

The changesets' `Skills-docs:` line still reads `follow-up owed` while the PR body names `follow-up #30731`; the seat says a prose-only commit brings them to the same text — outside this record's judgment, noted so the next head's reader sees it.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Round-1 must-fix — fixed (④).
- Round-1 should-fix, object ladder — fixed, with one residual (④).
- Round-1 should-fix, multi-select clause — fixed: `OPTION_ARGUMENT_RULE` (template-engine.ts:263-268) ends "A multi-select value prints the label of each of its values, joined with `, `, and a value outside the field's options prints as stored", the spec quotes it word for word (email-template.zod.ts:126-130, pinned on all three faces), the regenerated reference page carries it on all three rows, the spec changeset restates it. True against the formatter (:174-175). Right.
- os-dev-report 6673314821: `open_questions` empty; the round-1 out-of-scope item is resolved by the ladder. The window re-measurement (render and send both throw, the recording transport received nothing) matches the tree: plugin-email's render (template-engine.ts:161) calls `formatValue`, which throws; `sendTemplate` rethrows anything not prefixed `TEMPLATE_INVALID` (email-service.ts:1607), so nothing is sent.
- Carried to card #30730 (the server half, plugin-email's surface, not this PR's): in the window the refusal surfaces as a bare `RangeError` from `formatValue`, outside the `TEMPLATE_INVALID` vocabulary the `IEmailService` contract states; the server half asks `optionTableRefusal` before `formatValue` and prefixes `TEMPLATE_INVALID`, exactly as plugin-email asks `currencyDefaultRefusal` (template-engine.ts:147) — the function was exported for that call.
- Check-runs on `d73ae610` at review time: 62 success (Build Core / Docs / UI Deps, Type Check ×6, Lint ×8, Test Core 1-3 and 5-8, Test UI ×17, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Dogfood Regression Gate, Live E2E UI, …), 10 skipped, 1 pending (a second `Check Changeset` run in progress), and 2 failure: `Test Core (4/8)` and its aggregate `Test Core`. The red shard is one test, `packages/cli/test/validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts` "the command sources use no call shape this scan cannot read", failed by `Test timed out in 5000ms` (no assertion), in a cli suite that reported 714 s of import time on that runner; the test scans cli command sources, this PR changes nothing under `packages/cli`, the only main-side change to that file since the merge-base is a ledger row (#30712), and main `447226b2` is green on all eight shards. A red gate verdict stands as red: the PR needs a green re-run of that shard before it lands, which the seat's hold for #30730 already implies. Not a finding against the diff.

### ④ Design judgment

`hits`: packages/spec/src/system/email-template.zod.ts:126-130. Against ruling F parameters 1, 2, 4 and the spec side of 5: holds (carried). Against its first consumer at this head: holds now — a hole the sentence says prints a label either prints it from the table the renderer hands in or is refused; the stored value is never printed in its place (template-engine.ts:169-173, pinned at test.ts:196-203 for no table, a table for another field, a string, an array and a null value; the refusal sentence pinned at :206-226, including an inherited-only key and a key holding no table). The formatter comment (:160-168), the formula changeset bullet, the docs paragraph (email-templates.mdx:164-171) and the `formatValue` doc say the same thing. In the window nothing published is false: the docs' "the renderer builds the label table … in the locale it renders that recipient's copy in" (:164-165) and the spec's "prints the label … in the recipient's language" are the end state #30730 delivers, and until it lands every such hole is refused with a sentence naming the hole, the field and the rule, and nothing is sent — main's send-side outcome for the same hole today. The seat's back-to-back landing closes the window; nothing in this tree needs to change for it.

Round-1 must-fix: **fixed**. Round-1 should-fix 3 (multi-select clause): **fixed**.

Round-1 should-fix 2 (object ladder): **fixed** for rungs ①, ③ and the sibling-package case, with one residual —

**SHOULD-FIX** — packages/lint/src/validate-email-template-hole-grammar.ts:136-138 with packages/formula/src/mail-hole-grammar.ts:176-182. The ladder this arm now names (validate-object-references.ts:256-275) has a fourth rung: a platform-prefixed name (`sys_`, `cloud_`, `ai_`) no known package registers and the stack does not define is a `warning` (`object-reference-unregistered-platform`, "a third-party package still might" register it), never an error. The option arm refuses it at `error` (`sys_userz` is pinned as refused at lint test.ts:94-95). So `os validate` and `os build` block a template naming a third-party platform-prefixed object that the publish door, judging the live universe, would accept — the same CLI-vs-publish gap round 1 named, now confined to rung ④. Fix: for a name with a platform prefix that is in none of the three resolved sets, emit the ladder's advisory (`warning`, the `object-reference-unregistered-platform` sentence or the arm's own, with the field unjudged) instead of `option-object-unknown` at error, and pin `sys_userz` as a warning rather than an error; the publish door and #30730's `TEMPLATE_INVALID` keep the real refusal. Small, no verdict change.

Tried and holding on the delta: `optionTableRefusal` with `undefined`, `null`, a table without the key, a key holding `null`, an inherited-only key → the refusal; a key holding `{}` → null (an empty option list is the server half's `TEMPLATE_INVALID`, not this formatter's); `formatValue('option', …, undefined)` with no argument → the refusal names `option:` and an empty field (unreachable from a mail face, where `option-field-shape` refuses first); a `packages[]` entry with no `manifest`, or `manifest` not an object → skipped, as `validate-object-references.ts` skips it; a sibling package re-declaring a stack object → the stack's definition wins (`!index.has`); the in-app engine never reaches `FORMATTERS.option` (compile refuses first, carried).
